title: What mass spectrometry measures
summary: From molecules to ions to evidence: understand what a mass spectrum can—and cannot—tell you.
text: The central idea Mass spectrometry (MS) studies matter by producing gas-phase ions and measuring signals associated with their mass-to-charge ratios, written m/z . A neutral molecule must become an ion before it can be manipulated by electric fields. The detected ion is not necessarily the original molecule: it may have gained a proton, acquired an adduct , or broken into fragments. IUPAC provides the terminology used throughout this wiki. [1] A mass spectrum places m/z on the horizontal axis and signal intensity on the vertical axis. Each peak represents an ion population within a small measurement interval. It is evidence about a sample, interpreted through an instrument and a method. [1] The base peak is the most intense peak in a spectrum. [3] When a plot uses base-peak relative intensity, that peak is set to 100% and each other peak is scaled by relative intensity (%) = 100 × peak intensity / base-peak intensity . The denominator is the strongest peak in that same spectrum, not the sum of all peaks. [4] A 50% peak therefore has half the base peak's signal; it does not mean half the molecules or half the sample. Follow the measurement Prepare and introduce the sample. Extraction, dilution, and chromatography determine which material reaches the source. Form ions. Ionization chemistry determines which charged species are produced. Transfer and analyze. Ion optics transmit part of that population; an analyzer distinguishes ions by m/z . Detect and process. Detector signals become peaks, chromatographic features, and candidate identifications. In liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), spectra are acquired repeatedly as compounds elute. A spectrum describes a moment or time interval; a chromatogram follows signal over time. An extracted ion chromatogram (XIC) follows signal in a selected m/z interval over time. [5] These views answer different questions. Read across for a spectrum, down for a trace Constructed three-scan example: a scan is one spectral measurement. Imagine three scans collected during chromatography with unchanged acquisition settings. All peaks are listed below; their positions and intensities are invented. Intensities use the same arbitrary signal scale, before any per-scan normalization. No chemical identities are assigned. Each row is one spectrum; time is measured from injection Time / min Signal at m/z 100.000 Signal at m/z 200.000 Signal at m/z 300.000 1.0 20 100 10 2.0 80 40 20 3.0 40 20 80 One spectrum: read the 2.0 min row across. Plot peaks at m/z 100.000, 200.000, and 300.000 with intensities 80, 40, and 20. Its horizontal axis is m/z . One XIC: select m/z 100.000 ± 0.010, meaning the inclusive interval 99.990–100.010. For this exercise, sum the recorded peak signals in that interval at each time. Only the 100.000 peak is included, so reading its column down gives 20, 80, and 40 at 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 min. The XIC's horizontal axis is time. These three points illustrate the two views, not validated chromatographic sampling or peak integration. Check the denominator: the base peaks lie at m/z 200.000, 100.000, and 300.000 in the three scans; their intensities are 100, 80, and 80. If each spectrum is separately scaled to its own base peak, the 100.000 peak becomes 100 × 20 / 100 = 20% , 100 × 80 / 80 = 100% , and 100 × 40 / 80 = 50% . Those percentages use changing denominators. The XIC above uses the original 20, 80, and 40 signals instead. Keep the intensity scale with the data; relative peak heights alone cannot establish concentration. Worked example: one compound, several peaks Separate constructed mass example: suppose a neutral compound has a monoisotopic mass of 300.0000 Da, calculated using the most abundant isotope of each element. In positive electrospray ionization (ESI) it might produce a protonated ion, [M+H] + , near m/z 301.0073 and a sodium adduct, [M+Na] + , near 322.9892. Heavier isotopes can add further peaks. Several peaks therefore need not mean several compounds. The rounded positions use a proton mass of 1.007276467 Da and a sodium-cation mass of approximately 22.989220702 Da; both ions have charge +1. [6] [7] See the adduct calculation for the electron-mass correction. Conversely, two compounds can produce ions at the same nominal or even exact m/z . Structural isomers can share a formula. Separation, fragmentation, standards, and other evidence help distinguish them. Signal is not automatically concentration Response depends on ionization efficiency, matrix effects, transmission, acquisition settings, and detector behavior. A peak twice as high does not by itself establish twice the concentration across different compounds. Quantification needs a defined response model, suitable calibration, quality controls, and often an internal standard. Reference spectra help evaluate identity, but the ionization and fragmentation conditions must be compatible. NIST maintains distinct electron-ionization and tandem-MS reference libraries, reflecting that difference. [2] Check your understanding Does the tallest peak have to be the molecular ion? No. It is the base peak—the most intense peak in that spectrum. It could be a fragment, an adduct, a contaminant, or another ion. Its intensity alone does not establish identity. Beyond the basics For computational work, keep the measurement layers separate: a centroid peak, a chromatographic feature, an ion assignment, and a molecular identification are different objects. Trace every processed result back to the scan, sample, and processing parameters that produced it.

title: 质谱测量的是什么
summary: 从分子到离子，再到证据：理解质谱能够回答和无法单独回答的问题。
text: 核心概念 质谱（MS）通过生成气相离子并测量与其质荷比（ m/z ）相关的信号来研究物质。中性分子需要先转变为离子，才能被电场操控。检测到的离子不一定就是原始分子：它可能接受了质子、形成了 加合物 ，或发生了碎裂。本知识库的术语以 IUPAC 的建议为基础。 [1] 质谱图 的横轴是 m/z ，纵轴是信号强度。每个峰表示一个较小测量区间内的离子群。质谱是关于样品的证据，需要结合仪器与实验方法解释。 [1] 基峰 是某张质谱图中强度最高的峰。 [3] 当谱图采用相对于基峰的强度时，将基峰设为 100%，其他峰按 相对强度（%）= 100 × 峰强度 / 基峰强度 缩放。分母是同一张谱图中最强峰的强度，不是所有峰强度之和。 [4] 因此，50% 的峰表示其信号为基峰的一半，并不表示它占分子数或样品量的一半。 沿着测量流程理解 样品处理与引入。 提取、稀释和色谱分离决定哪些物质到达离子源。 形成离子。 电离过程决定产生哪些带电物种。 传输与分析。 离子光学系统传输其中一部分离子，质量分析器按 m/z 区分它们。 检测与处理。 检测信号转换为谱峰、色谱特征和候选鉴定结果。 在液相色谱–质谱（LC–MS）中，化合物洗脱时仪器连续采集质谱。质谱图描述某个时刻或时间区间；色谱图描述信号随时间的变化。 提取离子色谱图（XIC） 跟踪选定 m/z 范围内的信号随时间的变化。 [5] 它们回答不同的问题。 横向读取谱图，纵向读取时间轨迹 构造的三次扫描示例： 一次扫描就是一次谱图测量。假设在色谱过程中，以不变的采集设置进行了三次扫描。下表列出了全部峰；峰位置和强度均为虚构。强度使用同一任意信号尺度，尚未按每次扫描单独归一化。这里不指认任何化学身份。 每一行是一张质谱图；时间从进样时开始计算 时间 / min m/z 100.000 处的信号 m/z 200.000 处的信号 m/z 300.000 处的信号 1.0 20 100 10 2.0 80 40 20 3.0 40 20 80 一张质谱图： 横向读取 2.0 min 这一行。在 m/z 100.000、200.000 和 300.000 处分别画出强度为 80、40 和 20 的峰。横轴是 m/z 。 一条 XIC： 选择 m/z 100.000 ± 0.010，即包含端点的 99.990–100.010 区间。在本练习中，对每个时间点落入该区间的记录峰信号求和。这里仅包含 100.000 处的峰，因此纵向读取该列，可得 1.0、2.0 和 3.0 min 时的信号分别为 20、80 和 40。XIC 的横轴是时间。这三个点用于说明两种数据视图，并不代表已验证的色谱采样或峰积分方法。 检查分母： 三次扫描的基峰分别位于 m/z 200.000、100.000 和 300.000，强度分别为 100、80 和 80。如果每张谱图分别按自身基峰缩放，100.000 处的峰就依次变为 100 × 20 / 100 = 20% 、 100 × 80 / 80 = 100% 和 100 × 40 / 80 = 50% 。这些百分比使用了不同的分母。上面的 XIC 则使用原始的 20、80 和 40 信号。应保留数据所用的强度尺度；仅凭相对峰高不能确定浓度。 计算示例：一个化合物，多个峰 另一个构造的质量计算示例： 假设某中性化合物的 单同位素质量 是 300.0000 Da，即采用各元素丰度最高的同位素计算的质量。在正离子电喷雾电离（ESI）中，它可能形成质子化离子 [M+H] + ，位于 m/z 301.0073 附近；也可能形成钠加合离子 [M+Na] + ，位于 322.9892 附近。较重同位素还会产生其他峰。因此，多个峰并不一定代表多个化合物。上述舍入后的位置采用质子质量 1.007276467 Da 和近似钠阳离子质量 22.989220702 Da；两种离子的电荷均为 +1。 [6] [7] 电子质量修正见 加合离子计算示例 。 反过来，不同化合物也可能形成标称质荷比甚至精确质荷比相同的离子。结构异构体可以具有相同分子式。分离、碎裂、标准品及其他证据有助于区分它们。 信号不直接等于浓度 响应受到电离效率、基质效应、传输、采集设置和检测器行为的影响。对于不同化合物，峰高相差两倍并不能直接证明浓度相差两倍。定量需要明确的响应模型、合适的校准和质量控制，通常还需要内标。 参考谱图可以帮助评价身份，但电离和碎裂条件需要匹配。NIST 分别维护电子电离和串联质谱参考库，体现了二者的区别。 [2] 理解检查 最高的峰一定是分子离子峰吗？ 不是。它是基峰，即该谱图中强度最高的峰。它可能是碎片、加合物、污染物或其他离子。仅靠强度不能确定其身份。 进一步学习 在计算分析中，应区分质心峰、色谱特征、离子指认和分子鉴定这几个层次。每个处理结果都应该能够追溯到对应的扫描、样品和处理参数。

title: m/z, charge & isotopes
summary: Calculate charged-ion masses and build an isotope distribution, then connect both to measurement quality.
text: Start with the ion, not the neutral molecule An ion’s mass and charge jointly determine its position on a mass spectrum. The conventional horizontal coordinate m/z is dimensionless: divide the ion mass expressed in daltons by the magnitude of its charge number. It is not the physical ratio in kg/C, and an axis labeled m/z should not be labeled Da. State positive or negative polarity separately. This follows the IUPAC convention. [1] For the arithmetic below, let x denote that numerical coordinate, M the neutral monoisotopic mass, μ = M/Da its numerical value, and n = |z| the positive integer charge magnitude. Let h = 1.007276467 , the proton mass in Da rounded from NIST CODATA. [3] We neglect binding-energy mass corrections at this teaching precision. Proton-only ion formulas; M refers to the same neutral species Ion Coordinate x Recover neutral mass M [M+nH] n+ (μ + nh) / n (nx − nh) Da [M−nH] n− (μ − nh) / n (nx + nh) Da These expressions describe addition or removal of protons. A sodium adduct, a radical ion formed by electron loss, and a mixed-adduct ion require different compositions. Do not substitute the neutral hydrogen-atom mass (about 1.007825032 Da) for the proton mass. Neutral hydrogen includes an electron; the difference is about 0.0005486 Da. The atomic-mass and particle-mass tables describe different entities. [2] [3] Worked example: one mass, several charge states Assume a hypothetical neutral species with M = 1000.000000 Da forms only protonated ions. The predicted positions are: Ion n Predicted m/z [M+H] + 1 1001.007276 [M+2H] 2+ 2 501.007276 [M+3H] 3+ 3 334.340610 Use the unrounded coordinate for inverse calculations: M = (2 × 501.007276467 − 2 × 1.007276467) Da = 1000.000000 Da . A triply deprotonated ion of the same assumed neutral mass would instead occur near m/z 332.326057. Negative polarity does not require plotting a negative horizontal coordinate. The lower-positioned ion need not be the smaller molecule. Equally, one isolated peak cannot determine both mass and charge: charge needs independent evidence, such as a resolved isotope pattern or related charge states. Isotope spacing helps infer charge Replacing one 12 C by 13 C adds 1.00335483507 Da. Thus, for corresponding carbon-isotope peaks of the same ion, Δx = 1.00335483507 / n . NIST supplies the isotope masses. [4] At n = 1, 2, and 3, the spacings are about 1.003355, 0.501677, and 0.334452, respectively. Compare several intervals before assigning charge; overlapping envelopes or missing peaks can mimic another spacing. An isotopologue differs in isotope composition. The monoisotopic mass is the exact mass calculated using the most abundant isotope of each element. For another specified isotopic composition, calculate that isotopologue’s exact mass . [1] The average mass weights isotope compositions by abundance. The monoisotopic peak is not necessarily the base peak (the most intense peak). Do not use an average mass as a monoisotopic search target. Build an isotope distribution from probabilities Here is an intentionally simplified model: a molecule has N carbon atoms, each independently 13 C with fixed probability p = 0.0107 and otherwise 12 C. Hold all other elements at fixed isotopes and ignore radioactive carbon. The value of p is a representative NIST composition, not a universal constant for every sample. [4] If K is the number of 13 C atoms, its binomial probability is P(K=k) = C(N,k) pᵏ (1−p)ᴺ⁻ᵏ , for integers 0 ≤ k ≤ N. Here C(N,k) = N! / (k! (N−k)!) counts the possible placements. This is our calculation from the stated model, not an experimentally measured distribution. Carbon-only model: percentage of molecules in each isotope class Carbon atoms N k = 0 k = 1 k = 2 10 89.8008% 9.7126% 0.4727% 100 34.1037% 36.8856% 19.7478% Other k values hold the remaining probability. For N = 100, the k = 1 class is more abundant than k = 0: the monoisotopic peak is not the tallest in this model. Also distinguish a fraction of the total from a ratio to the monoisotopic peak . For N = 10, P(1)/P(0) = Np/(1−p) ≈ 0.108157 ; the M+1 signal is about 10.8157% of M, not 9.7126% of M. The labels M, M+1, and M+2 here denote nominal isotope classes, not exact increments of 1 Da or 1 in m/z . A real molecular envelope combines isotopes of every element. For example, M+2 can include two 13 C atoms replacing two 12 C atoms, or one 18 O replacing 16 O, at different exact masses. [2] Sufficient resolving power can reveal this isotope fine structure; an unresolved nominal class can contain several contributions. Connect the pattern to measurement quality Charge inference depends on peak separation. A narrow-looking centroid stick has no displayed profile width, so it cannot establish resolving power. Likewise, a plausible isotope pattern does not certify the absolute mass calibration. See resolving power versus mass accuracy for definitions and the annotated simulated spectrum to combine charge, isotope ratios, and mass error. Common misconceptions “Every peak is a compound.” One compound can produce several charge states, adducts, isotopologues, and fragments. “The first visible isotope peak must be monoisotopic.” The true monoisotopic peak may be below detection or obscured. “M+1 directly counts carbon atoms.” The approximation assumes a carbon-dominated, interference-free pattern with suitable abundance and response assumptions; other isotopes contribute in real samples. “An exact isotope match proves identity.” It supports a composition hypothesis, but structural isomers can share the same distribution. Check your understanding Three successive carbon-isotope peaks are about 0.3345 apart. What is plausible, and what remains unknown? Charge magnitude 3 is plausible because 1.00335483507 / 3 ≈ 0.334452. Polarity, adduct composition, the monoisotopic assignment, and molecular identity still need evidence. The spacing alone does not supply them. Beyond the basics Deisotoping groups isotopic peaks of an ion. Charge deconvolution combines evidence across charge states to estimate neutral masses. Preserve the original data and document isotope models, abundance assumptions, tolerances, and adduct rules. Neither operation by itself establishes a molecular identity.

title: 质荷比、电荷与同位素
summary: 计算带电离子的质量并构建同位素分布，再将二者与测量质量联系起来。
text: 从离子出发，而不是从中性分子出发 离子的质量和电荷共同决定它在质谱图上的位置。常用横坐标 m/z 无量纲：将以道尔顿表示的离子质量数值除以电荷数绝对值。它不是以 kg/C 表示的物理比值，标为 m/z 的轴不应再标 Da。正负极性应单独说明。这遵循 IUPAC 的约定。 [1] 下文计算中， x 表示这一坐标数值， M 是中性单同位素质量， μ = M/Da 是其数值， n = |z| 是正整数电荷数绝对值。令 h = 1.007276467 ，即由 NIST CODATA 质子质量取舍得到的以 Da 为单位的数值。 [3] 在这一教学精度下，忽略结合能对应的质量修正。 仅加减质子的离子公式；M 对应同一中性物种 离子 坐标 x 还原中性质量 M [M+nH] n+ (μ + nh) / n (nx − nh) Da [M−nH] n− (μ − nh) / n (nx + nh) Da 这些公式描述加入或移除质子。钠加合物、失去电子形成的自由基离子及混合加合物需要使用不同组成。不要用中性氢原子质量（约 1.007825032 Da）代替质子质量。中性氢包含一个电子，二者相差约 0.0005486 Da。原子质量表与粒子质量表描述的是不同实体。 [2] [3] 计算示例：一种质量，多个电荷态 假设某中性物种的 M = 1000.000000 Da，并且只形成质子化离子。预测位置如下： 离子 n 预测 m/z [M+H] + 1 1001.007276 [M+2H] 2+ 2 501.007276 [M+3H] 3+ 3 334.340610 逆向计算使用未舍入坐标： M = (2 × 501.007276467 − 2 × 1.007276467) Da = 1000.000000 Da 。同一假定中性质量的三重去质子化离子则位于 m/z 332.326057 附近。负极性并不要求横坐标使用负数。 位置更低的离子不一定来自更小的分子。同样，一个孤立峰无法同时确定质量和电荷：需要已分辨的同位素模式或相关电荷态等独立证据来判断电荷。 同位素间距帮助推断电荷 用一个 13 C 替代 12 C，质量增加 1.00335483507 Da。因此，同一离子对应碳同位素峰间的坐标差为 Δx = 1.00335483507 / n 。同位素质量来自 NIST。 [4] 当 n = 1、2、3 时，间距分别约为 1.003355、0.501677、0.334452。赋予电荷前应比较多个间隔；包络重叠或峰缺失可能模拟出另一种间距。 同位素体 在同位素组成上不同。 单同位素 质量是使用各元素最丰度同位素计算的精确质量。对于其他指定同位素组成，应计算该同位素体的 精确质量 。 [1] 平均 质量按丰度对同位素组成加权。单同位素峰不一定是基峰，即强度最高的峰。不要用平均质量作为单同位素搜索目标。 从概率构建同位素分布 考虑一个刻意简化的模型：分子有 N 个碳原子，每个原子独立地以固定概率 p = 0.0107 为 13 C，否则为 12 C。其他元素均固定为指定同位素，忽略放射性碳。p 采用 NIST 的代表性组成，并不是所有样品都适用的普适常数。 [4] 若 K 为 13 C 原子数，其二项分布概率为 P(K=k) = C(N,k) pᵏ (1−p)ᴺ⁻ᵏ ，其中 k 是 0 ≤ k ≤ N 的整数。 C(N,k) = N! / (k! (N−k)!) 表示可能的排列位置组合数。这是根据已说明模型进行的计算，并非实验测得的分布。 仅考虑碳同位素的模型：各类占分子总数的百分比 碳原子数 N k = 0 k = 1 k = 2 10 89.8008% 9.7126% 0.4727% 100 34.1037% 36.8856% 19.7478% 其余概率分布在其他 k 值上。N = 100 时，k = 1 的类别比 k = 0 更丰度，因此模型中的单同位素峰不是最高峰。还要区分 占总数的比例 和 相对于单同位素峰的比值 。N = 10 时， P(1)/P(0) = Np/(1−p) ≈ 0.108157 ；M+1 信号约为 M 的 10.8157%，不是 M 的 9.7126%。 这里的 M、M+1 和 M+2 表示标称同位素类别，不表示精确增加 1 Da，也不表示 m/z 增加 1。真实分子包络综合了各元素的同位素。例如，M+2 中可以包含两个 13 C 替代两个 12 C 的贡献，或一个 18 O 替代 16 O 的贡献，二者精确质量不同。 [2] 足够的分辨本领可以揭示这种同位素精细结构；未分辨的标称类别则可能合并多种贡献。 将模式与测量质量联系起来 电荷推断依赖峰的分离。看起来很细的质心棒图并未显示轮廓峰宽，因此不能据此确定分辨本领。同样，合理的同位素模式不能证明绝对质量校准准确。定义请参阅 分辨本领与质量准确度 ；结合电荷、同位素比值和质量误差的练习见 带注释的模拟谱图 。 常见误解 “每个峰都是一个化合物。” 一个化合物可以产生多个电荷态、加合物、同位素体和碎片。 “第一个可见同位素峰一定是单同位素峰。” 真正的单同位素峰可能低于检测限或被遮蔽。 “M+1 可以直接给出碳原子数。” 这种近似要求碳主导、无干扰的模式，以及合适的丰度与响应假设；真实样品中其他同位素也会贡献信号。 “同位素完全匹配就能证明身份。” 它支持组成假设，但结构异构体可以具有相同分布。 理解检查 连续三个碳同位素峰间距约 0.3345，可以推断什么，还有什么未知？ 电荷数绝对值为 3 是合理假设，因为 1.00335483507 / 3 ≈ 0.334452。但极性、加合物组成、单同位素峰指认和分子身份仍需要证据。间距本身不能给出这些答案。 进一步学习 去同位素处理对同一离子的同位素峰进行分组；电荷去卷积则结合不同电荷态的证据估计中性质量。应保留原始数据，并记录同位素模型、丰度假设、容差与加合物规则。两种处理都不能独立确立分子身份。

title: How molecules become ions
summary: Compare ESI, MALDI, EI, and APCI by the chemistry they enable—not by a universal ranking.
text: The source shapes what you see A mass analyzer needs gas-phase ions. The ion source connects the sample to that measurement: it helps release charged species into the gas phase, and its chemistry influences which ion forms survive. One compound can therefore give several signals, while another compound in the same sample may give little signal. Two questions make a useful starting point: How did the source produce this ion? and What composition and charge does the ion have? ESI and MALDI are often described as soft ionization methods, meaning that extensive fragmentation can be avoided. “Soft” does not promise that every analyte stays intact under every source or transfer condition. [1] Compare sources by the sample and the question Typical starting points; these are tendencies rather than exclusive application boundaries Method Starting material and process Practical consequence Electrospray ionization (ESI) A solution forms a spray of charged droplets, from which gas-phase ions emerge. Fits continuous liquid delivery, including LC. Polar or ionizable small molecules, peptides, and proteins are common targets; multiple charge states are especially important for large molecules. Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) A laser illuminates analyte associated with a light-absorbing matrix, often on a prepared target. Fits spot-based analysis and spatial sampling, including imaging. Conventional peptide MALDI often favors singly charged ions; matrix and preparation strongly affect the result. Electron ionization (EI) Energetic electrons interact with gas-phase molecules. Common with GC for sufficiently volatile, thermally stable compounds. Radical molecular cations and fragments are possible; the molecular ion can be weak or absent. Atmospheric-pressure chemical ionization (APCI) Vaporized sample encounters reagent ions, commonly generated using a corona discharge. A useful LC option for some analytes less suited to ESI, provided they tolerate vaporization and the gas-phase chemistry is favorable. These source names describe ion production, not the mass analyzer: MALDI does not mean TOF, and ESI does not mean a particular analyzer. Source definitions follow IUPAC; the ESI and MALDI qualifications are developed below. [1] ESI: from charged droplets to gas-phase ions A potential difference between the liquid emitter and another electrode drives electrospray. Solvent evaporation reduces droplet size; electrostatic repulsion can then destabilize droplets and produce smaller ones. Drying gas, temperature, flow rate, solvent, and the interface influence this journey. This is more than simply adding a proton to every molecule. Different models describe the final release of ions. In the ion evaporation model , small solvated ions leave a charged droplet surface. In the charged residue model , evaporation of the remaining solvent leaves an analyte carrying charge. In the chain ejection model , an extended polymer chain progressively emerges from the droplet. These models help explain different analytes and conditions; they should not be presented as one universal sequence that every ESI ion follows. [3] For proteins, compact structures under native-like conditions are commonly discussed using charged-residue behavior, whereas unfolded chains under denaturing conditions can follow chain ejection. Charging also depends on additives and experimental conditions, so a charge-state distribution is not by itself a unique report of solution structure. [4] Multiple charging is a major reason ESI makes large biomolecules accessible: dividing the ion mass by a larger charge magnitude moves the signal to lower m/z . Fenn and colleagues demonstrated characteristic sequences of different charge states for large biomolecules. [2] Several such peaks may represent the same neutral species, rather than several proteins. MALDI: the matrix is part of the experiment In common ultraviolet MALDI, the matrix absorbs laser energy and assists release of sample material. The expanding plume contains interacting species, including neutrals and ions. Primary ion formation and subsequent reactions, such as proton or cation transfer, both matter. Mechanistic descriptions differ in how the first charges arise and how clusters participate; a single “the laser gives the molecule a proton” story misses that chemistry. [5] Conventional MALDI peptide spectra often contain mainly singly protonated ions, which can make charge interpretation simpler. [6] This is a useful expectation, not a rule that MALDI can only make +1 ions. Other charge states and adducts can occur, and specialized atmospheric-pressure matrix-assisted laser methods have produced highly multiply charged peptide and protein ions. [7] MALDI can be operated in positive or negative polarity; the matrix, analyte, and conditions influence which ions are useful. [12] Matrix-related ions can crowd the low- m/z region. Crystal distribution, analyte incorporation, and laser conditions can change the signal from one location to another. A matrix blank and replicate sampling are therefore important checks. Avoid assuming that MALDI is immune to contaminants or suppression simply because it can tolerate some preparations that cause difficulty in ESI. [5] [6] Studies of MALDI peptides have directly demonstrated interfering alkali-metal adduct and matrix-cluster signals. [13] Read polarity, composition, and charge separately Positive-ion mode records cations; negative-ion mode records anions. The sign tells you the ion's net charge, not whether it gained or lost an electron in one particular reaction. For example, a neutral molecule can gain H + to form a positive ion or lose H + to form a negative ion. In the notation below, M denotes the same neutral molecule , and the superscript outside the brackets gives the net charge. [1] Common ion-form hypotheses; actual formation depends on the compound and conditions Ion notation Charge How to read it [M+H] + +1 Protonated molecule: M plus one proton. [M−H] − −1 Deprotonated molecule: M minus one proton. [M+Na] + +1 Sodium adduct: M associated with Na + . [M+NH 4 ] + +1 Ammonium adduct: M associated with NH 4 + . [M+Cl] − −1 Chloride adduct: M associated with Cl − . [M+2H] 2+ / [M−2H] 2− +2 / −2 Two protons added or removed; one M, charge magnitude 2. [M+H+Na] 2+ +2 A mixed ion form containing one added proton and one sodium cation. [2M+H] + +1 A protonated cluster containing two M units; the 2 before M does not mean charge 2. Use “protonated molecule” for [M+H] + . A molecular radical cation M +• , commonly encountered in EI, instead has lost an electron without adding a proton. These species have different compositions and masses. Permanently charged analytes require their own charge bookkeeping; the neutral-M examples are not a universal description of all ions. [1] Solution composition helps determine which possibilities are plausible. Sodium contamination or salts can favor sodium adducts; ammonium-containing additives can support ammonium adducts. [1] [13] An acidic or basic functional group may suggest a polarity to test, but neither its presence nor the source name guarantees the dominant ion. Keep the solvent, additives, polarity, and source settings with the spectrum. Recover the neutral mass from an explicit ion assignment Use x for the numerical m/z coordinate, M for the neutral monoisotopic mass, μ = M/Da , and n = |z| for the charge magnitude. The coordinate is dimensionless; polarity is stated separately. Monoisotopic mass uses the most abundant isotope of each element. First establish the monoisotopic peak and charge rather than substituting the tallest peak or an average mass. See the charge and isotope guide . [1] For an assigned ion containing k copies of M and a net added mass of δ Da , the bookkeeping is x = (kμ + δ) / n , so M = ((nx − δ) / k) Da . A removed proton contributes a negative δ. This is our mass-balance calculation, conditional on the stated ion formula. Approximate mass inputs in Da; retained digits support reproducible arithmetic, not nine-decimal measurement accuracy Species Mass used Basis H + 1.007276467 Proton mass, rounded from NIST CODATA 2022. 23 Na + 22.989220702 23 Na atom mass minus one electron mass. 14 N 1 H 4 + 18.033825553 14 N + four 1 H atom masses minus one electron mass. 35 Cl − 34.969401262 35 Cl atom mass plus one electron mass. The last three values are calculated from NIST neutral-atom isotope masses and the CODATA electron mass, about 0.000548579909 Da. Binding-energy mass corrections are neglected at this teaching precision. A neutral 1 H atom has mass about 1.007825032 Da: using that in place of H + introduces an electron-sized error. Do not subtract an electron again when you already used an ionic mass. [8] [9] Worked examples: one assumed mass, several ion forms These are constructed calculations, not measured peaks or a proposed compound. Assume a neutral monoisotopic mass of 300.000000 Da, the isotope choices above, and no isotope-labeling or neutral-loss complications. The table shows where each ion would occur if it formed ; it does not predict that one real sample will produce them all. Positions are rounded to six decimals, but the inverse calculations retain the nine-decimal inputs. Calculated positions for the hypothetical neutral mass Assigned ion n δ Predicted m/z [M+H] + 1 +1.007276467 301.007276 [M+Na] + 1 +22.989220702 322.989221 [M+NH 4 ] + 1 +18.033825553 318.033826 [M−H] − 1 −1.007276467 298.992724 [M+Cl] − 1 +34.969401262 334.969401 [M+2H] 2+ 2 +2.014552934 151.007276 [M−2H] 2− 2 −2.014552934 148.992724 [M+H+Na] 2+ 2 +23.996497169 161.998249 [2M+H] + 1 +1.007276467 601.007276 A. A sodium assignment changes the subtraction For the proposed sodium adduct, M = (322.989220702 − 22.989220702) Da = 300.000000 Da . If you incorrectly call it [M+H] + , you obtain 321.981944235 Da. That 21.981944235 Da discrepancy comes from the wrong ion model, not from poor mass calibration. The predicted singly charged sodium and protonated forms are separated by 21.981944235 in m/z . Replacing one proton with sodium in a doubly charged ion gives half that separation, 10.990972118 after rounding. Always account for charge before applying a memorized adduct difference. B. Deprotonation requires adding the proton back For [M−H] − , M = (298.992723533 + 1.007276467) Da = 300.000000 Da . A chloride adduct instead requires subtracting the chloride-ion mass. Both are negative ions, but their mass corrections have opposite signs. C. Multiply by charge magnitude, then correct the composition For [M+2H] 2+ , M = (2 × 151.007276467 − 2 × 1.007276467) Da = 300.000000 Da . For [2M+H] + , first subtract the proton and then divide by two: M = ((601.007276467 − 1.007276467) / 2) Da = 300.000000 Da . The first ion has two charges on one M; the second has one charge on two M units. None of these successful inversions establishes a formula or structure. They show that an ion assignment is arithmetically consistent with an assumed neutral mass. Real assignments also need charge evidence, isotope consistency, suitable tolerances, and checks for competing explanations. Before concluding that a compound is absent Signal can change because of extraction, chromatography, ion production, transmission, or detection. Coeluting material and nonvolatile solutes can suppress ESI response; experiments on biological extracts have linked suppression to changes in droplet properties. This is one reason a peak's intensity is not a direct count of molecules in the original sample. [10] Check the method and the search target. Confirm polarity, mass range, scan type, plausible charge states, and candidate adducts. Check blanks and a suitable standard. Distinguish background from analyte-related signal; compare sample preparation and source conditions. Look for related evidence. Inspect isotope spacing, chromatographic peak shapes, and possible source fragments. Shared retention time helps but does not prove that peaks belong together. Test one controlled change. Dilution, cleanup, or a source-setting change may help investigate a problem, but any one result can have several explanations. Record the change and compare appropriate controls. Common interpretation traps “Positive mode means [M+H] + .” Sodium, ammonium, mixed adducts, and already charged species are alternatives. “Negative mode means the molecule gained an electron.” Deprotonation and anion attachment can also produce negative ions. “A lower m/z means a smaller neutral molecule.” A higher charge magnitude can move a large ion to a lower coordinate. “MALDI always gives one peak and ESI always gives many charges.” Both depend on analyte and conditions; isotope peaks and adducts can add complexity even at charge 1. “An adduct pair proves the compound's identity.” It supports a relationship hypothesis. Coelution, isomers, overlapping signals, and incorrect charge assignments remain possible. Check your understanding Two positive-ion peaks are 21.981944 apart. Can you immediately call them [M+H]+ and [M+Na]+? No. That separation is consistent with the singly charged pair, but first establish charge and test whether their isotope patterns and chromatographic behavior support a shared origin. Unrelated peaks can have a similar difference. Can a soft source produce a fragment that looks like another analyte? Yes. Fragmentation can occur in the source or interface before precursor selection. Check related ions, retention behavior, and controlled source-condition changes; a fragment signal alone does not establish a second compound. Does subtracting 1.007276467 from every peak recover neutral masses? No. That operation fits a singly protonated monomer only. Charge, adduct composition, neutral losses, clusters, and the chosen isotope peak all matter. Connect ion assignment to stronger evidence Use the assigned ion form when selecting a precursor and interpreting MS/MS . Protonated and sodium-adducted forms need not fragment alike. EI reference spectra and ESI tandem spectra are not interchangeable; NIST maintains separate EI and tandem library collections. [11] Computational grouping should retain polarity, charge, isotope assignment, adduct rules, and the original observations. Grouping related features can simplify a dataset, but it does not itself identify a structure. Continue with step-by-step spectrum interpretation to combine those hypotheses with independent evidence.

title: 分子如何变成离子
summary: 根据电离过程与适用化学性质比较 ESI、MALDI、EI 和 APCI。
text: 离子源决定了你能看到什么 质量分析器需要气相离子。离子源把样品与测量过程连接起来：它帮助带电物种进入气相，其化学过程也影响哪些离子形式能够保留下来。因此，同一种化合物可能产生多个信号，而同一样品中的另一种化合物可能几乎没有信号。 可以先问两个问题： 离子源如何产生了这个离子？ 以及 这个离子具有怎样的组成和电荷？ ESI 和 MALDI 常被称为软电离方法，表示可以避免大规模碎裂。但“软”并不保证所有分析物在任何离子源或传输条件下都保持完整。 [1] 根据样品和分析问题比较离子源 常见选择起点；这些是一般倾向，并非排他的应用边界 方法 起始材料与过程 实际意义 电喷雾电离（ESI） 溶液形成带电液滴喷雾，随后产生气相离子。 适合包括 LC 在内的连续液体进样。常用于极性或可电离的小分子、肽和蛋白质；分析大分子时，多电荷态尤其重要。 基质辅助激光解吸/电离（MALDI） 激光照射与吸光基质结合的分析物，样品通常位于制备好的靶板上。 适合点样分析和空间采样，包括成像。常规肽 MALDI 往往以单电荷离子为主；基质和制样方式会显著影响结果。 电子电离（EI） 高能电子与气相分子相互作用。 常与 GC 联用，适合具有足够挥发性和热稳定性的化合物。可以产生分子自由基阳离子及碎片；分子离子可能很弱或缺失。 大气压化学电离（APCI） 气化后的样品与试剂离子接触，试剂离子通常由电晕放电产生。 对于某些不太适合 ESI 的分析物，它是有用的 LC 联用选择，前提是分析物能够耐受气化，且气相化学过程适宜。 这些离子源名称描述的是离子生成方式，而非质量分析器：MALDI 不等于 TOF，ESI 也不对应某一种特定分析器。离子源定义依据 IUPAC；下文将进一步说明 ESI 和 MALDI 的适用条件与限制。 [1] ESI：从带电液滴到气相离子 液体喷射端与另一电极之间的电位差驱动电喷雾。溶剂蒸发使液滴缩小；静电排斥随后可能使液滴失稳，形成更小的液滴。干燥气、温度、流速、溶剂及接口都会影响这一过程。它并非只是给每个分子加上一个质子。 不同模型描述了离子最终脱离液滴的过程。在 离子蒸发模型 中，小的溶剂化离子从带电液滴表面逸出。在 带电残余模型 中，剩余溶剂蒸发后留下带电的分析物。在 链排出模型 中，伸展的聚合物链逐步从液滴中伸出。这些模型有助于解释不同分析物和条件下的行为，不应被描述成每个 ESI 离子都必然经历的一套统一步骤。 [3] 对于蛋白质，类天然条件下的紧凑结构通常用带电残余行为来讨论，而变性条件下的展开链可能遵循链排出过程。带电程度也受添加剂和实验条件影响，因此，仅凭电荷态分布无法唯一确定溶液中的结构。 [4] 多电荷是 ESI 能够分析大生物分子的重要原因：离子质量除以更大的电荷数绝对值，信号便移至较低的质荷比位置。Fenn 等人展示了大生物分子具有代表性的不同电荷态峰序列。 [2] 其中多个峰可能对应同一种中性物种，而非多种蛋白质。 MALDI：基质是实验的一部分 在常见的紫外 MALDI 中，基质吸收激光能量，并辅助样品物质释放。膨胀的羽流中包含相互作用的物种，包括中性物种和离子。初级离子形成及随后的质子转移、阳离子转移等反应都很重要。不同机理描述对最初电荷如何产生、团簇如何参与有不同解释；只用“激光给分子一个质子”来描述，会遗漏这些化学过程。 [5] 常规 MALDI 肽谱往往以单质子化离子为主，这可以简化电荷判断。 [6] 这是有用的一般预期，并不表示 MALDI 只能生成 +1 离子。其他电荷态和加合物也可能出现，某些专门的大气压基质辅助激光方法已经产生了带多个电荷的肽和蛋白质离子。 [7] MALDI 可在正、负离子模式下运行；基质、分析物和实验条件共同影响哪些离子具有分析价值。 [12] 基质相关离子可能使低质荷比区域变得拥挤。晶体分布、分析物在基质中的分布以及激光条件，都可能使不同位置的信号发生变化。因此，基质空白和重复采样是重要的检查手段。即使 MALDI 能够耐受某些会给 ESI 带来困难的制样条件，也不能据此认为它不受污染物或离子抑制影响。 [5] [6] 对 MALDI 肽谱的研究已直接展示碱金属加合物和基质团簇信号所产生的干扰。 [13] 分别读取极性、组成和电荷 正离子模式记录阳离子，负离子模式记录阴离子。符号表示离子的净电荷，而非某一种特定反应中是否得失了电子。例如，中性分子可以获得 H + 而形成正离子，也可以失去 H + 而形成负离子。在下列记号中， M 表示同一个中性分子 ，方括号外的上标表示净电荷。 [1] 常见离子形式假设；实际能否形成取决于化合物和实验条件 离子记号 电荷 含义 [M+H] + +1 质子化分子：M 加上一个质子。 [M−H] − −1 去质子化分子：M 失去一个质子。 [M+Na] + +1 钠加合离子：M 与 Na + 结合。 [M+NH 4 ] + +1 铵加合离子：M 与 NH 4 + 结合。 [M+Cl] − −1 氯离子加合物：M 与 Cl − 结合。 [M+2H] 2+ / [M−2H] 2− +2 / −2 获得或失去两个质子；包含一个 M，电荷数绝对值为 2。 [M+H+Na] 2+ +2 混合离子形式，额外包含一个质子和一个钠阳离子。 [2M+H] + +1 包含两个 M 单元的质子化团簇；M 前的 2 不表示电荷数为 2。 [M+H] + 应称为“质子化分子”。EI 中常见的分子自由基阳离子 M +• 则是失去一个电子而没有增加质子的产物，两者的组成和质量不同。永久带电的分析物需要单独核算电荷；以中性 M 为起点的示例不能概括所有离子。 [1] 溶液组成有助于判断哪些离子形式合理。钠污染或盐可能促进钠加合离子的形成；含铵添加剂可能有利于铵加合离子的形成。 [1] [13] 酸性或碱性官能团可以提示优先尝试哪种极性，但官能团的存在和离子源名称都不能保证某种离子一定占主导。应随谱图一并保留溶剂、添加剂、极性和离子源参数。 根据明确的离子归属反推中性质量 用 x 表示质荷比坐标的数值， M 表示中性单同位素质量， μ = M/Da ， n = |z| 表示电荷数的绝对值。该坐标无量纲，极性另行说明。单同位素质量使用每种元素丰度最高的同位素计算。应先确定单同位素峰和电荷，不能直接代入最高峰的位置或平均质量。参见 电荷与同位素指南 。 [1] 如果所归属的离子包含 k 个 M 单元，净增加的质量为 δ Da ，则有 x = (kμ + δ) / n ，因此 M = ((nx − δ) / k) Da 。每移去一个质子，都对 δ 贡献一个负的质量变化。这是依据所给离子式进行的质量守恒计算，结论以该离子式成立为前提。 以 Da 表示的近似质量输入；保留位数用于复现运算，不表示测量准确到小数点后九位 物种 采用的质量 依据 H + 1.007276467 NIST CODATA 2022 质子质量的舍入值。 23 Na + 22.989220702 23 Na 原子质量减去一个电子质量。 14 N 1 H 4 + 18.033825553 14 N 与四个 1 H 原子质量之和减去一个电子质量。 35 Cl − 34.969401262 35 Cl 原子质量加上一个电子质量。 后三个数值由 NIST 中性原子同位素质量和 CODATA 电子质量计算得到；电子质量约为 0.000548579909 Da。在本教学精度下忽略结合能对应的质量修正。中性 1 H 原子的质量约为 1.007825032 Da，用它替代 H + 会引入约一个电子质量的误差。如果已经使用离子质量，就不要再次扣除电子质量。 [8] [9] 计算示例：同一个假定质量，多种离子形式 以下是人为构造的计算，不是实测峰，也没有提出某个具体化合物。 假设中性单同位素质量为 300.000000 Da，采用上述同位素组成，不考虑同位素标记或中性丢失等复杂情况。表中给出各离子形式 如果形成 时所在的位置，并不预测某个真实样品会产生所有这些离子。坐标保留六位小数，反算时则保留输入值的九位小数。 假定中性质量所对应的计算位置 归属的离子 n δ 预测的 m/z [M+H] + 1 +1.007276467 301.007276 [M+Na] + 1 +22.989220702 322.989221 [M+NH 4 ] + 1 +18.033825553 318.033826 [M−H] − 1 −1.007276467 298.992724 [M+Cl] − 1 +34.969401262 334.969401 [M+2H] 2+ 2 +2.014552934 151.007276 [M−2H] 2− 2 −2.014552934 148.992724 [M+H+Na] 2+ 2 +23.996497169 161.998249 [2M+H] + 1 +1.007276467 601.007276 A. 钠加合归属会改变应减去的质量 对于假定的钠加合离子， M = (322.989220702 − 22.989220702) Da = 300.000000 Da 。如果错误地将其归为 [M+H] + ，则会得到 321.981944235 Da。这一 21.981944235 Da 的差异来自错误的离子模型，而非质量校准不良。 预测的单电荷钠加合离子与质子化分子在质荷比上的间隔为 21.981944235。若在 双电荷 离子中用一个钠替换一个质子，间隔则为其一半，舍入后为 10.990972118。应用记忆中的加合物质量差之前，务必先考虑电荷。 B. 去质子化后需要把质子质量加回去 对于 [M−H] − ， M = (298.992723533 + 1.007276467) Da = 300.000000 Da 。氯离子加合物则需要减去氯离子质量。两者都是负离子，但质量修正的符号相反。 C. 先乘以电荷数绝对值，再修正组成 对于 [M+2H] 2+ ， M = (2 × 151.007276467 − 2 × 1.007276467) Da = 300.000000 Da 。对于 [2M+H] + ，先减去质子质量，再除以二： M = ((601.007276467 − 1.007276467) / 2) Da = 300.000000 Da 。前者是一个 M 带两个电荷，后者是两个 M 单元共同带一个电荷。 这些反算即使完全吻合，也不能确定分子式或结构。它们只能说明某个离子归属与假定的中性质量在算术上相容。真实归属还需要电荷证据、同位素一致性、适当的容差，以及对其他可能解释的检查。 认定化合物不存在之前 提取、色谱分离、离子生成、传输和检测环节都可能导致信号变化。共洗脱物和不挥发溶质可以抑制 ESI 响应；对生物提取物的实验将这种抑制与液滴性质的变化联系起来。这也是峰强度不能直接等同于原始样品中分子数量的原因之一。 [10] 检查方法和搜索目标。 确认极性、质量范围、扫描类型、合理的电荷态和候选加合物。 检查空白和适当的标准品。 区分背景与分析物相关信号，并比较制样方式和离子源条件。 寻找相关证据。 检查同位素间隔、色谱峰形及可能的源内碎片。保留时间一致有帮助，但不能证明多个峰必然属于同一物种。 每次检验一个受控变化。 稀释、净化或调整离子源参数可能有助于排查问题，但任何单一结果都可能有多种解释。应记录变化，并使用适当对照进行比较。 常见解释误区 “正离子模式就表示 [M+H] + 。” 钠加合物、铵加合物、混合加合物和本身已经带电的物种都是其他可能。 “负离子模式表示分子得到了一个电子。” 去质子化和阴离子结合也可以产生负离子。 “质荷比更低，中性分子就更小。” 更大的电荷数绝对值可以使大离子移到更低的坐标位置。 “MALDI 总是只有一个峰，ESI 总是有许多电荷态。” 两者都取决于分析物和条件；即使电荷数为 1，同位素峰和加合物也可能增加复杂性。 “一对加合离子就能证明化合物身份。” 它支持的是峰之间关联的假设。共洗脱、异构体、信号重叠和错误电荷归属仍然可能存在。 理解检查 两个正离子峰相隔 21.981944，可以立即归为 [M+H]+ 和 [M+Na]+ 吗？ 不能。这个间隔与上述单电荷离子对相容，但首先应确定电荷，并检验同位素模式和色谱行为是否支持共同来源。不相关的峰也可能具有相似的间隔。 软电离源能否产生看起来像另一种分析物的碎片？ 可以。碎裂可能在前体选择之前发生于离子源或接口。应检查相关离子、保留行为以及受控的离子源条件变化；仅有一个碎片信号不足以确认存在第二种化合物。 从每个峰的位置减去 1.007276467，就能得到中性质量吗？ 不能。该操作只适用于单质子化的单体。电荷、加合组成、中性丢失、团簇和所选同位素峰都会影响计算。 把离子归属与更强的证据结合起来 选择前体及解释 MS/MS 时，应使用所归属的离子形式。质子化分子和钠加合形式不一定以相同方式碎裂。EI 参考谱与 ESI 串联谱不能互换；NIST 分别维护 EI 和串联质谱库。 [11] 计算分组应保留极性、电荷、同位素归属、加合物规则及原始观测。把相关特征分组可以简化数据集，但这一操作本身不能鉴定结构。继续阅读 逐步解读质谱图 ，学习如何把这些假设与独立证据结合起来。

title: Mass analyzers & resolution
summary: Follow quadrupole filtering, TOF timing, ion trapping, and frequency measurement, then compare resolution and accuracy.
text: Different physics, the same coordinate A mass analyzer relates ion motion to m/z . It does not identify a compound by itself. Instruments often combine analyzers: a quadrupole may select a precursor, a collision cell may fragment it, and a time-of-flight or Orbitrap analyzer may measure products. For each analyzer, ask three questions: what happens to the ions, what signal is measured, and how is that signal converted into m/z ? Read the overview first, then work through the mechanisms before comparing performance. Compare mechanisms Analyzer Physical idea What to watch Quadrupole Radio-frequency and direct-current fields allow selected ion trajectories to remain stable. Useful as a mass filter. Isolation width and transmission affect selectivity and sensitivity. Time of flight (TOF) After controlled acceleration, flight time depends on mass-to-charge ratio. Timing, initial energy spread, calibration, and ion optics affect peak width and accuracy. RF ion trap Fields confine ions; controlled excitation or ejection enables analysis and multiple stages of fragmentation. Ion capacity, space charge, scan conditions, and accessible mass range matter. Orbitrap Axial oscillation frequencies in an electrostatic field encode m/z . Signal observation time and ion population affect performance. FT-ICR Cyclotron motion in a magnetic field produces frequencies related to m/z . Magnetic field, transient duration, and ion interactions influence resolving power. IUPAC defines these analyzer families. [1] Makarov's original Orbitrap paper describes the electrostatic trapping and frequency-based mass-analysis principle. [2] Quadrupole: a stability filter Four rods form a passage for ions. Opposite rods share a voltage; the two rod pairs receive opposite combinations of a direct-current (DC) voltage and an alternating radio-frequency (RF) voltage. For a chosen setting, a band of m/z values has stable transverse motion in both directions and can pass through. Other trajectories grow too large to be transmitted. This is a test of motion in an electric field, not a chemical recognition step. [4] In a conventional mass scan at a fixed RF frequency, the instrument changes RF and DC amplitudes together so that the transmitted band moves across the chosen range. Recording detector signal against that changing setting builds a spectrum. Holding selected settings instead enables selected-ion monitoring. [5] A fixed isolation window can pass several different ions; selecting a nominal m/z does not establish molecular identity. Do not infer the function from four rods alone. An RF-only quadrupole can guide a broad band above a low- m/z cutoff without the narrow RF/DC filtering described here. Such ion guides and collision-cell devices have different jobs. [6] Time of flight: turn arrival time into m/z A TOF experiment launches an ion packet and records when ions arrive at a detector. Under controlled starting conditions, lower- m/z ions arrive earlier. A pulse defines the time origin; this can come from pulsed ion formation or pulsed extraction of an existing ion beam. [7] Ideal teaching model: assume negligible initial kinetic energy, an acceleration potential difference of magnitude V, a field-free path of length L, and nonrelativistic motion without collisions. Let M be the physical ion mass, n = |z| the positive charge-number magnitude, e the elementary charge, and u the dalton expressed as a physical mass. For the numerical spectral coordinate x = M / (u n) , energy conservation gives M v² / 2 = n e V . Substituting τ = L / v yields τ = L √(u x / (2 e V)) , so x ∝ τ² . Ions accelerated through the same V receive the same energy per charge , not necessarily the same total energy. Constructed ratio example: if x = 100 has a corrected flight time τ = 10 microseconds, the same ideal setup gives 20 microseconds at x = 400 and 30 microseconds at x = 900. Four times the m/z gives twice the flight time. In a calibrated instrument, the measured time may include an offset: use τ = t − t₀ , not t blindly. Real packets have spreads in position, energy, and launch time. A reflectron is an electrostatic ion mirror: at the same m/z , higher-energy ions penetrate farther and spend longer in the mirror, which can compensate for some flight-time spread. [7] Actual ion optics and calibration are more elaborate than the straight-path teaching equation; it is not a universal instrument calibration formula. RF ion traps: store, select, activate, and eject An RF ion trap confines ions for a controlled period. A linear quadrupole trap can analyze them by changing trapping and excitation conditions so that different m/z groups leave for detection in sequence. It can also isolate ions, activate them, keep selected products, and repeat the sequence for MS n . These operations are demonstrated in the primary linear-trap study. [8] Storage makes a sequence of experiments possible within one device, but stored ions are not independent of one another. Their mutual electrical repulsion is called space charge ; it changes motion when the population becomes too dense. [9] Ion population, scan conditions, and the chosen trapping/activation settings therefore belong in a method description. Here “RF ion trap” means the quadrupole-trap family. Orbitrap and FT-ICR instruments also trap ions, but the frequency-based detection described below differs from mass-selective ejection. Frequency analysis: listen to repeated ion motion Moving ion packets induce small electrical signals in nearby electrodes. An image-current measurement records this signal while ions remain in the analyzer, rather than requiring each ion to strike a detector. The resulting time record is a transient . Fourier transformation separates its frequency components, then a calibration relation maps frequency to m/z . This workflow underlies both Orbitrap and FT-ICR measurements. [10] [11] Orbitrap: measure axial oscillation Ions orbit a central electrode while oscillating along its axis in an electrostatic field. The frequency used for mass analysis is the axial oscillation frequency , not simply the rate of travel around the electrode. In the ideal field, f = C / √x , where x is the numerical m/z and C is fixed by the analyzer field and geometry. [2] Constructed example: choose C so that x = 200 gives f = 100 kHz. At x = 800, f is 50 kHz. Thus x = (C / f)² : increasing m/z decreases frequency. These chosen values teach the relationship and are not specifications for an instrument. FT-ICR: measure motion in a magnetic field A magnetic field bends an ion's motion. For ideal, nonrelativistic free cyclotron motion perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of magnitude B, equating magnetic and centripetal forces gives n e v B = M v² / r . With f_c = v / (2πr) and the definitions above, f_c = e B / (2π u x) . At fixed B, the unperturbed cyclotron frequency is proportional to 1 / x . In FT-ICR, excitation organizes ion motion for a measurable time-domain signal, followed by Fourier analysis. [11] A real ICR cell also uses electric trapping fields; the commonly detected reduced cyclotron frequency differs from the ideal free frequency. Practical calibration must account for the actual measurement conditions. [12] Separate constructed example: choose B so the ideal f c is 100 kHz at x = 200. At x = 800 it is 25 kHz. The Orbitrap example above drops by a factor of two; this ideal ICR example drops by a factor of four. The different exponents matter when interpreting performance across a mass range. Observation time is one part of acquisition time Close frequencies become easier to distinguish when a useful, coherent signal is observed for longer. A simple mathematical scale is the unpadded discrete Fourier transform grid: for N samples at sampling frequency f s , T = N / f_s and Δf_grid = f_s / N = 1 / T . A 0.10-second record has 10 Hz grid spacing; a 0.20-second record has 5 Hz. This is grid spacing, not a universal FWHM or a guaranteed two-peak separation . Adding zeros to the same recorded sequence makes the computed frequency grid denser without observing ions for longer. Signal decay, noise, and the processing method still affect the peak you obtain. Actual Fourier processing can change reported resolving power at the same recorded duration; a primary instrument study demonstrates the importance of phase information. [13] Transient duration also differs from ion accumulation time and the complete acquisition cycle. Loading, isolation, activation, readout, and other events can contribute; some instruments overlap operations. [13] Check the actual cycle timing when deciding how often a chromatographic peak is sampled. Follow the ion through a hybrid instrument Read a hybrid instrument description as a sequence of jobs: make ions → select or transmit ions → optionally activate them → measure the resulting ions . The quadrupole in a Q-TOF or quadrupole–Orbitrap arrangement can select an incoming band; the later analyzer measures the ions that emerge from the experiment. “High-resolution MS/MS” therefore does not, by itself, specify a narrow precursor isolation window. See Fragmentation & tandem MS for the selection-to-product sequence and Mass analyzer for the terminology. Worked example: a resolution claim A specification states R = 50,000 at m/z 500 using full width at half maximum (FWHM). Let x be the numerical m/z coordinate and w the profile peak width on that same coordinate scale, measured between the two half-height crossings after baseline subtraction. Then R = x / w and w = 500 / 50,000 = 0.010 . R is dimensionless. The width here is a difference in m/z coordinates, not a neutral mass in Da. FWHM and a two-peak valley criterion are different measurement conventions; a resolution number without its convention and reference m/z is incomplete. [1] Two ions separated by 0.004 near 500 may not be adequately distinguished at this width. The ratio 500 / 0.004 = 125,000 merely sets a width scale equal to their separation; it does not guarantee baseline separation. Peak shape, relative intensity, and signal quality matter. Resolving power, mass accuracy, and precision Resolving power concerns the width or separation of peaks. Mass accuracy concerns closeness to a reference value; signed mass error measures a particular deviation. Precision concerns agreement among repeated measurements. Calibration and interference affect the reliability of measured positions, even when peaks are narrow. Official instrument guidance discusses why accuracy must be evaluated under defined conditions. [3] Define x obs as an observed coordinate and x ref as the reference for the same ion composition, charge, and isotope . Then error (ppm) = 10⁶ × (x_obs − x_ref) / x_ref . A positive value means the measured position is too high. Comparing a protonated ion to a neutral mass or the wrong isotope gives a meaningless accuracy assessment. Constructed comparisons at reference m/z 500.0000; FWHM measured from profile data Case Observed m/z FWHM w R = x_obs / w Signed error Narrow, offset 500.0020 0.0100 ≈ 50,000 +4 ppm Broad, centered 500.0000 0.1000 5,000 0 ppm The second case illustrates a zero error for one idealized measurement, not a demonstrated instrument accuracy specification. Repeated positions of 500.0019, 500.0020, and 500.0021 are tightly grouped but still biased high. Repeatability does not remove systematic error, and one favorable measurement cannot establish performance across a mass range. A matching window is not a peak width For a chosen tolerance t in ppm, a symmetric search window around x ref has half-width δ = x_ref × t × 10⁻⁶ . At 500, ±5 ppm means ±0.0025, or 499.9975–500.0025. At 1000, the same tolerance means ±0.0050. A fixed coordinate window and a fixed ppm window therefore behave differently across the spectrum. A tolerance is an analysis decision, not a statement that every accepted match is correct. Do not infer it from the number of displayed decimal places. Use calibration evidence, suitable controls, and the distribution of errors under the relevant method. A centroid list alone does not retain the profile width needed for a FWHM measurement. See the annotated simulated example for a separate view of position offset and width. Performance is a set of tradeoffs Longer transients can improve frequency discrimination in Fourier-transform measurements, but take time. In an LC experiment, the instrument must still sample the chromatographic peak often enough. Higher nominal resolving power is not automatically the best acquisition choice. Mass accuracy concerns deviation from a reference value. Resolving power concerns peak separation. Sensitivity concerns response to analyte amount under a defined method. Dynamic range concerns the usable signal span. Compare them under stated conditions, not as a single ranking of instruments. Check your understanding Does high resolving power eliminate a co-isolated precursor? No. Precursors can enter the same isolation window before high-resolution product measurement. Better product separation can help interpretation, but does not undo the mixed fragmentation event. Does a TOF ion with twice the mass always arrive later? No. Compare m/z , not mass alone. In the ideal model, an ion of mass 800 u and charge magnitude 2 has the same x = 400 as an ion of mass 400 u and charge magnitude 1, so both have the same flight time under the stated conditions. Does doubling the displayed Fourier grid density double the observation time? No. Zero filling can increase the number of plotted frequency points from the same recorded signal. A longer physical transient requires additional measured samples over a longer time. Beyond the basics Centroiding, Fourier processing, calibration, and peak fitting can change the reported peak list. For algorithm evaluation, retain the acquisition settings and distinguish profile data from centroid data. A benchmark on one analyzer and processing pipeline need not transfer unchanged to another.

title: 质量分析器与分辨率
summary: 理解四极杆过滤、TOF 计时、离子俘获与频率测量，再比较分辨本领与准确度。
text: 不同物理机制，相同坐标 质量分析器 将离子运动与 m/z 联系起来，但它本身不能确定化合物身份。仪器常组合多种部件：四极杆选择前体，碰撞池使其碎裂，飞行时间或 Orbitrap 分析器测量产物离子。 对于每种分析器，可以先问三个问题：离子经历什么运动，测量什么信号，又如何把信号转换为 m/z ？先看概览，再理解机制，最后比较性能。 比较分析机制 分析器 物理原理 需要注意 四极杆 射频与直流电场使选定离子的运动轨迹保持稳定。 可作为质量过滤器。隔离宽度和传输效率影响选择性与灵敏度。 飞行时间（TOF） 受控加速后，飞行时间与质荷比相关。 计时、初始能量分布、校准和离子光学影响峰宽与准确度。 射频离子阱 电场约束离子，通过受控激发或排出来分析，也可进行多级碎裂。 离子容量、空间电荷、扫描条件和可用质量范围很重要。 Orbitrap 静电场中的轴向振荡频率编码质荷比。 信号观察时间和离子数量影响性能。 FT-ICR 磁场中的回旋运动产生与质荷比相关的频率。 磁场、瞬态信号时长和离子相互作用影响分辨本领。 IUPAC 对这些分析器类型作出了定义。 [1] Makarov 的原始 Orbitrap 论文介绍了静电俘获与基于频率的质量分析原理。 [2] 四极杆：利用运动稳定性过滤离子 四根杆电极围成离子通道。相对的两根杆连接同一电压；两组杆上施加符号相反的直流（DC）与射频（RF）交流电压组合。在给定设置下，某一 m/z 范围内的离子在两个横向方向上均保持稳定运动，因而能够通过；其他离子的运动幅度过大，无法传输。这检验的是电场中的运动，而不是识别化学物质身份。 [4] 在 RF 频率固定的常规质量扫描中，仪器同时改变 RF 与 DC 的幅度，使可传输的范围沿选定区间移动。将检测器信号与变化的设置对应起来，即可形成质谱图。保持在选定设置则可进行选择离子监测。 [5] 固定的隔离窗口可能同时通过多种离子；选中某个标称 m/z 并不能确定分子身份。 不能仅凭“四根杆”就判断其功能。 仅射频四极杆 可传输低 m/z 截止值以上较宽范围的离子，并不进行上述 RF/DC 窄带过滤。因此，离子导向器和碰撞池中的这类器件承担的任务不同。 [6] 飞行时间：由到达时间换算 m/z TOF 实验发射一个离子包，并记录离子到达检测器的时间。在起始条件受控时，较低 m/z 的离子先到达。脉冲确定计时起点；它可以来自脉冲式离子产生，也可以来自对已有离子束的脉冲提取。 [7] 理想教学模型： 假设初始动能可忽略，加速电势差的大小为 V，无场飞行路径长度为 L，离子以非相对论速度运动且不发生碰撞。令 M 为离子的实际质量，n = |z| 为电荷数的正值大小，e 为元电荷，u 为表示实际质量的道尔顿。谱图坐标数值为 x = M / (u n) ；能量守恒给出 M v² / 2 = n e V 。代入 τ = L / v 得到 τ = L √(u x / (2 e V)) ，因此 x ∝ τ² 。经过相同 V 加速的离子获得相同的 单位电荷能量 ，不一定获得相同的总能量。 构造的比例示例： 若 x = 100 时，经修正的飞行时间 τ = 10 微秒，则同一理想装置在 x = 400 时给出 20 微秒，在 x = 900 时给出 30 微秒。 m/z 增至四倍，飞行时间增至两倍。实际仪器的测量时间可能含有偏移：应使用 τ = t − t₀ ，不能直接把 t 代入。 真实离子包的初始位置、能量和发射时间均存在分布。 反射器（reflectron） 是一种静电离子镜：对于相同 m/z ，能量较高的离子进入镜场更深、停留更久，从而补偿部分飞行时间差。 [7] 实际离子光学与校准关系比直线路径教学方程更复杂；该方程不是通用的仪器校准公式。 射频离子阱：储存、选择、活化与排出 射频离子阱将离子限制在器件内一段受控时间。线性四极杆离子阱可改变俘获和激发条件，使不同 m/z 的离子依次排出并接受检测。它还可以隔离离子、使其活化、保留选定产物，再重复这一过程，实现 MS n 。原始线性离子阱研究演示了这些操作。 [8] 离子储存使同一器件内的一系列实验成为可能，但被储存的离子并非彼此独立。离子间的相互电排斥称为 空间电荷 效应；当离子群过于密集时，其运动会受到影响。 [9] 因此，离子数量、扫描条件以及俘获和活化设置都应写入方法说明。 本节的“射频离子阱”指四极杆离子阱这一类。Orbitrap 和 FT-ICR 也会俘获离子，但下文基于频率的检测方式不同于质量选择性排出。 频率分析：记录反复的离子运动 运动的离子包会在附近电极上感应出微弱电信号。 镜像电流 测量在离子仍处于分析器内时记录该信号，不需要每个离子撞击检测器。这段时间记录称为 瞬态信号 。傅里叶变换分解出其中的频率分量，再通过校准关系将频率转换为 m/z 。Orbitrap 与 FT-ICR 都采用这一基本流程。 [10] [11] Orbitrap：测量轴向振荡 离子在静电场中绕中心电极运行，同时沿其轴向振荡。用于质量分析的是 轴向振荡频率 ，而非简单地测量绕电极转动的速率。在理想电场中， f = C / √x ，其中 x 为 m/z 数值，C 由分析器电场与几何结构决定。 [2] 构造示例： 选取 C，使 x = 200 时 f = 100 kHz，则 x = 800 时 f = 50 kHz。因此 x = (C / f)² ： m/z 越高，频率越低。这里选取的数值仅用于说明关系，不是某台仪器的指标。 FT-ICR：测量磁场中的运动 磁场使离子运动轨迹弯曲。对于在大小为 B 的均匀磁场中、垂直于磁场方向的理想非相对论自由回旋运动，将磁力与向心力相等可得 n e v B = M v² / r 。结合 f_c = v / (2πr) 和前述定义，可得 f_c = e B / (2π u x) 。在 B 固定时，无扰动回旋频率与 1 / x 成正比。 FT-ICR 通过激发使离子运动形成可测量的时域信号，再进行傅里叶分析。 [11] 真实 ICR 池还使用俘获电场；通常检测到的约化回旋频率不同于理想的自由回旋频率。实际校准必须考虑真实测量条件。 [12] 另一个独立的构造示例： 选取 B，使 x = 200 时理想 f c 为 100 kHz，则 x = 800 时为 25 kHz。前面的 Orbitrap 示例下降至二分之一，而本理想 ICR 示例下降至四分之一。不同的指数关系会影响对不同质量范围内性能的理解。 观察时间只是采集时间的一部分 在有效、相干的信号能够持续时，观察越久通常越有利于区分相近频率。一个简单的数学尺度是未补零离散傅里叶变换的频率网格：若以采样频率 f s 记录 N 个样本，则 T = N / f_s ，且 Δf_grid = f_s / N = 1 / T 。0.10 秒记录对应 10 Hz 网格间距，0.20 秒记录对应 5 Hz。这里是 网格间距，不是通用的半高全宽，也不保证两个峰能够分开 。 在同一段记录后补零，可以加密计算得到的频率网格，却没有延长对离子的实际观察。信号衰减、噪声及处理方法仍影响最终峰形。在相同记录时长下，实际傅里叶处理也可能改变所报告的分辨本领；一项原始仪器研究展示了相位信息的重要性。 [13] 瞬态信号时长也不同于离子累积时间和完整采集周期。装载、隔离、活化、读出及其他步骤均可能占用时间；某些仪器会使部分操作重叠进行。 [13] 判断色谱峰被采样得是否足够密集时，应检查实际周期时间。 沿离子路径理解混合仪器 可将混合仪器的描述拆成一系列任务： 产生离子 → 选择或传输离子 → 按需活化 → 测量所得离子 。Q-TOF 或四极杆–Orbitrap 中的四极杆可选择进入的离子范围，后续分析器则测量实验产生的离子。因此，仅说“高分辨 MS/MS”并没有说明前体隔离窗口有多窄。选择到产物的流程见 碎裂与串联质谱 ，术语见 质量分析器 。 计算示例：解读分辨率指标 某指标给出在 m/z 500 处，采用半峰全宽（FWHM）定义时 R = 50,000。令 x 为质荷比坐标数值，w 为同一坐标尺度上的轮廓峰宽，即扣除基线后两个半峰高交点之间的距离。于是 R = x / w ，且 w = 500 / 50,000 = 0.010 。R 无量纲；这里的峰宽是质荷比坐标差，不是以 Da 表示的中性质量。 FWHM 与两峰之间的谷高标准是不同的测量约定；若未说明定义及参考质荷比，单独的分辨率数值是不完整的。 [1] 在此峰宽下，500 附近相差 0.004 的两个离子可能无法充分区分。500 / 0.004 = 125,000 只是给出一个峰宽等于峰间距的尺度，不能保证基线分离。峰形、相对强度和信号质量都很重要。 分辨本领、质量准确度与精密度 分辨本领关注峰宽或峰的分离。质量准确度关注接近参考值的程度；带符号的质量误差衡量某次具体偏差。精密度关注重复测量之间的一致性。即使峰很窄，校准与干扰仍会影响位置的可靠性。官方仪器指南解释了为什么应在明确条件下评价准确度。 [3] 定义 x obs 为观测坐标， x ref 为 相同离子组成、电荷和同位素 的参考坐标。则 error (ppm) = 10⁶ × (x_obs − x_ref) / x_ref 。正值表示测量位置偏高。若将质子化离子与中性质量或错误同位素比较，所得准确度评价没有意义。 参考 m/z 为 500.0000 的构造比较；FWHM 从轮廓数据测量 情况 观测 m/z FWHM w R = x_obs / w 带符号误差 窄峰，但有偏移 500.0020 0.0100 ≈ 50,000 +4 ppm 宽峰，但中心准确 500.0000 0.1000 5,000 0 ppm 第二种情况只是一次理想化测量误差为零，并不代表已经验证了仪器准确度指标。重复位置 500.0019、500.0020 和 500.0021 十分集中，但仍整体偏高。重复性不能消除系统误差，单个有利结果也不能证明整个质量范围内的性能。 匹配窗口不是峰宽 给定以 ppm 表示的容差 t，以 x ref 为中心的对称搜索窗口半宽为 δ = x_ref × t × 10⁻⁶ 。在 500 处，±5 ppm 表示 ±0.0025，即 499.9975–500.0025；在 1000 处，同一容差表示 ±0.0050。因此，固定坐标窗口和固定 ppm 窗口在不同位置的行为不同。 容差是一项分析决策，并不意味着所有通过窗口的匹配都正确。不能从显示的小数位数推断容差。应参考校准证据、合适对照及相关方法下的误差分布。单独的质心列表不保留测量 FWHM 所需的轮廓峰宽。参阅 带注释的模拟例子 ，分别观察位置偏移与峰宽。 性能需要权衡 在傅里叶变换测量中，更长的瞬态信号通常有利于区分频率，但也消耗时间。LC 实验仍需对色谱峰进行足够密集的采样。因此，更高的标称分辨本领不一定是最优采集选择。 质量准确度关注相对于参考值的偏差；分辨本领关注峰的分离；灵敏度关注既定方法下分析物量与响应的关系；动态范围关注可用信号跨度。比较时应说明条件，而不是用一个指标给仪器排序。 理解检查 高分辨本领能排除共隔离前体吗？ 不能。在高分辨产物测量之前，多个前体可能已经进入同一隔离窗口。产物分离能力有助于解释，但不能撤销已发生的混合碎裂。 TOF 中质量大一倍的离子一定更晚到达吗？ 不一定。应比较 m/z ，而不是只比较质量。在理想模型中，质量为 800 u、电荷数大小为 2 的离子，与质量为 400 u、电荷数大小为 1 的离子，都具有 x = 400；在所述条件下，它们的飞行时间相同。 显示的傅里叶频率网格密度翻倍，是否意味着观察时间翻倍？ 不是。补零可以增加由同一段记录计算出的频率点数。真正更长的瞬态记录，需要在更长时间内获取额外的实测样本。 进一步学习 质心化、傅里叶处理、校准及峰拟合都可能改变最终峰列表。评价算法时应保留采集参数，并区分轮廓数据和质心数据。在某种分析器和处理流程上的基准结果，不一定能直接推广到另一种情况。

title: Fragmentation & tandem MS
summary: Trace precursor isolation, compare activation methods, and interpret charge-aware product and neutral-loss evidence.
text: Select → activate → measure Tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) adds a relationship: which ions can arise from an earlier ion population? A common product-ion experiment has three jobs. Instruments can perform them in different regions or at different times in a trap; MS/MS does not require two separate instruments. Other MS/MS scan types ask different questions. [1] Isolate: transmit or retain a chosen m/z window. A survey scan can guide the choice, or the method can use a predefined target or window. A precursor ion is the starting ion for the reaction being considered. Activate or react: collisions, electrons, photons, or other interactions can open reaction pathways. Only some ions may dissociate; some products can react again. Measure: a mass analyzer distinguishes the resulting ions by m/z . The recorded spectrum may include fragment ions and surviving precursor ions. An unreacted precursor is not a newly formed product. A product ion is a reaction outcome, a broader category than a fragment: a reaction can change charge without breaking the molecular skeleton. “Precursor” and “product” describe roles in a specified step. A product selected for another reaction becomes that step's precursor. [1] What the product spectrum leaves out Ordinary product-ion mass analysis records charged species within its usable range. A neutral coproduct has no peak in that ion spectrum. Peak intensity also depends on competing pathways, ion transmission, measurement settings, and response. A missing peak does not establish that its proposed chemical pathway is impossible. Keep the ionization method, polarity, precursor assignment, isolation width, activation settings, and product measurement range with the data. Activation changes the evidence Collision-based methods In collision-induced dissociation (CID), ion–gas collisions can convert some relative translational energy into internal excitation, followed by dissociation. Resonant excitation of stored ions and acceleration through a gas-filled collision region deliver energy differently. [1] Higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) is a beam-type collisional implementation ; it belongs within collision-based fragmentation. A primary instrument study explicitly contrasts beam-type HCD with resonant-excitation collisional activation. [4] Ion composition, charge, gas, energy, and reaction time affect which pathways compete. Increasing a collision-energy setting can change both the extent of fragmentation and secondary fragmentation; it does not simply reveal more copies of one fixed spectrum. Record the actual method and units. Equal displayed energy numbers, especially normalized settings, need not mean equivalent activation across instruments. Electron-based methods: a useful peptide example In electron capture dissociation (ECD) , a multiply charged positive ion captures an electron. In conventional positive-ion electron transfer dissociation (ETD) , a reagent anion transfers an electron to the cation. Foundational peptide experiments showed backbone fragmentation complementary to collisional methods and retention of some labile modifications. These are useful capabilities, not guarantees for every sequence or modification. [5] [2] The positive charge decreases by one upon electron capture or transfer, without removing a proton. For example, the immediate charge-reduced species from [M+3H] 3+ is [M+3H] 2+• , not [M+2H] 2+ . The dot denotes an unpaired electron; this is composition and charge bookkeeping, not an exact-mass calculation. Include the incoming electron or reagent ion when balancing the whole reaction. Electron transfer can also leave a charge-reduced species without separated fragments, often called electron transfer without dissociation (ETnoD). Sequence, charge state, conformation, and reaction conditions matter; supplemental activation can help in some experiments. There is no universal “ETD only works above 2+” rule: a primary supplemental-activation study examined doubly protonated peptides. [6] This section concerns common ECD/ETD peptide applications, not every electron-driven reaction or every small molecule. Electron ionization (EI), introduced in the ionization Guide , is a different experiment. A first look at peptide ions Peptides make a useful worked language for backbone cleavage. The letter records a cleavage type and the retained terminus; the subscript counts residues from that terminus. Charge and radical state are additional information. These peptide labels are not a universal naming system for small-molecule fragments. [7] Common peptide backbone labels, with qualified method associations Series Retained terminus Backbone bond Common context b N terminus Amide C(=O)–N Often useful in positive-ion collisional peptide spectra y C terminus Amide C(=O)–N Often useful in positive-ion collisional peptide spectra c N terminus N–C α Often useful with ECD/ETD z-type C terminus N–C α ECD/ETD often yields radical z • products; hydrogen-transfer variants need explicit labels These method associations describe common peptide observations, not exclusive products or guaranteed sequence coverage. [2] [5] [6] For an abstract four-residue peptide A–G–S–K, b 2 refers to an N-terminal two-residue product and y 2 to a C-terminal two-residue product. The subscript 2 is a residue count, not a charge. A superscript 2+ would state charge. This naming example predicts neither peak presence nor intensity. Spectra can contain other ion series, neutral losses, internal fragments, and multiple charge states. [7] A residue gap needs a charge assumption Constructed arithmetic: the monoisotopic alanine residue increment C 3 H 5 NO is 3 × 12 + 5 × 1.00782503223 + 14.00307400443 + 15.99491461957 = 71.03711378515 Da , using NIST isotope masses as fixed central-value teaching constants, without uncertainty propagation. [9] [10] [11] [12] This is the residue increment within a peptide, not the mass of free alanine. For consecutive assigned ions in one terminal series, with unchanged ion chemistry and no additional loss, that increment produces an m/z gap of 71.0371 at charge +1, or 35.5186 when both ions have charge +2. A matching gap alone proves neither alanine's position nor a complete sequence. A wrong series assignment, a skipped residue, a modification, or overlapping ions can give a misleading interpretation. Balance composition and charge before subtracting peaks For a closed dissociation channel, account for all atoms, charges, and any neutral products. For an ion–ion or electron reaction, include the other reactants too. Fragmentation can rearrange atoms; a plausible product formula need not correspond to cutting one bond in a drawing. Conventional exact-mass bookkeeping sums isotope masses and electron/proton corrections, neglecting the much smaller chemical binding-energy contribution at the precision used here. Constructed ion-mass example: suppose an isolated 1000.0000 Da ion with charge +2 splits into 600.0000 Da and 400.0000 Da ions, each +1, with no neutral or exchanged species. These are abstract bookkeeping inputs, not proposed formulas or measured peaks. Charge balances as +2 = +1 + +1 , and ion masses as 1000 = 600 + 400 . Yet the precursor is at m/z 500 and the products at 600 and 400. A product can have higher m/z than its precursor because its charge is lower. Let x be the numerical m/z coordinate and n = |z|. The ion mass in Da is numerically n × x . Subtracting two x values directly gives a mass difference only after the charge relationship and reaction chemistry are specified. See Charge state and m/z . Worked example: neutral loss A neutral loss removes an uncharged species during ion dissociation. In a simple channel P z → Q z + N , the ionic product retains the precursor's charge and N is neutral. [8] Assuming no other exchanged or lost species and consistent isotope assignments, m(N) / Da = n × (x_P − x_Q) . The mass of the neutral loss and the m/z shift have different roles. Constructed water-loss calculations, not observations: choose 1 H 2 16 O. Its mass is 2 × 1.00782503223 + 15.99491461957 = 18.01056468403 Da . [9] [10] Treat the following starting coordinates as exact model inputs; calculate before rounding. Separate teaching cases with charge retained and only water lost Precursor / product charge Precursor m/z m/z decrease Product m/z, four decimals +1 / +1 301.100000 18.01056468403 283.0894 +2 / +2 301.100000 9.005282342015 292.0947 Thus the original 301.1000 → 283.0894 singly charged example is consistent with water loss after rounding. If both ions were instead +2, a gap of 18.0106 would represent about 36.0212 Da under the same simple-loss assumptions. Do not call every 18-unit gap “water.” Even a compatible accurate loss mass identifies neither a unique structure nor the atom-by-atom mechanism; the neutral itself was not measured in this product-ion spectrum. Use a pattern, not one diagnostic-looking peak One window can produce a mixed spectrum Isolation can include several ionic forms, such as isotope peaks or different adduct and charge states. Ions from different analytes can also be coisolated and fragmented together; their combined MS/MS signals are commonly called a chimeric spectrum. A primary peptide study demonstrated this identification problem. An ordinary isotope envelope alone does not imply multiple analytes, and the study's measured prevalence is specific to its samples and settings. [13] Ideal window exercise: assume a perfectly rectangular, symmetric window centered at 500.2 with full width 1.0. Its bounds are 499.7–500.7, so ions at 500.2 and 500.6 both pass. Width 0.4 gives 500.0–500.4 and excludes 500.6 in this model. Real isolation profiles have instrument-dependent transmission and edges; narrowing a window does not guarantee chemical purity, especially for overlapping or isomeric ions. High resolving power during product measurement can separate some products, but cannot by itself tell which precursor made each one. Review the precursor region and isolation settings; use chromatographic behavior, additional separation, or a more selective experiment when appropriate. Broad-window mixture handling belongs with the DIA and acquisition discussion . A practical interpretation checklist Check the starting assignment: polarity, charge, adduct, isotope, and possible coisolation. Test several linked products: use composition and charge balance, plausible losses, and the appropriate molecular-class chemistry. Inspect contradictions: unexplained intense peaks may reflect a mixture, alternative pathways, or an incorrect candidate. Do not silently delete them to improve a score. Compare compatible reference data: match ion type and relevant activation conditions. NIST documents both EI and tandem reference collections. [3] State the remaining alternatives: combine fragmentation with retention evidence, standards, and other measurements where available. A shared fragment or loss supports a hypothesis; it rarely singles out one structure. Check your understanding A +2 precursor and a +2 product differ by 9.0053 in m/z. What does that suggest? Under the simple unchanged-charge loss model, the neutral mass difference is about 18.0106 Da, compatible with water. It is not proof of water's origin, a unique mechanism, or molecular identity. Must every product have lower m/z than the precursor? No. Charge can change or be divided among products. Compare ion masses and balance the full reaction rather than comparing m/z alone. Does one matching fragment prove a candidate structure? No. Assess the full evidence and plausible alternatives. Related compounds can share products, and a mixed spectrum can create misleading combinations. Beyond the basics Fragmentation trees, sequence database searches, spectral prediction, and de novo sequencing formalize these constraints. Evaluate candidate ranking separately from calibrated confidence. A model can rank a wrong candidate first when the correct structure or sequence is absent from its search space. Continue with spectrum interpretation and reliable data analysis .

title: 碎裂与串联质谱
summary: 跟踪前体隔离、比较活化方法，并结合电荷解释产物与中性丢失证据。
text: 选择 → 活化 → 测量 串联质谱（MS/MS）增加了一层关系：较早阶段的离子群体能够产生哪些离子？常见的 产物离子实验 包含三个环节。仪器可以在不同空间区域完成这些操作，也可以在离子阱内按时间顺序完成；MS/MS 并不要求两台独立仪器。其他 MS/MS 扫描类型回答的问题有所不同。 [1] 隔离： 传输或保留选定 m/z 窗口内的离子。可以根据调查扫描选择，也可以采用方法中预先设定的目标或窗口。 前体离子 是所讨论反应的起始离子。 活化或反应： 碰撞、电子、光子或其他相互作用可以开启反应途径。可能只有部分离子发生解离，某些产物还会继续反应。 测量： 质量分析器 按 m/z 区分得到的离子。记录的谱图可能同时包含碎片离子和残留前体离子。未反应的前体并不是新生成的产物。 产物离子 是反应的结果，其范围比碎片离子更广：反应可以只改变电荷而不切断分子骨架。“前体”和“产物”描述的是离子在某一步反应中的角色。若将产物选出并继续反应，它就成为下一步的前体。 [1] 产物离子谱没有记录什么 常规产物离子质量分析记录可用范围内的带电物种。中性伴生产物不会在这张离子谱中形成峰。峰强度还受到竞争反应途径、离子传输、测量设置及响应的影响。缺少某个峰，不能直接证明所提议的化学途径不可能发生。应随数据保留电离方法、极性、前体指认、隔离宽度、活化设置和产物测量范围。 活化方式改变证据 碰撞类方法 在碰撞诱导解离（CID）中，离子与气体碰撞，可以将部分相对平动能转为内能激发，随后发生解离。对储存离子进行共振激发，与将离子加速通过充气碰撞区域，传递能量的方式不同。 [1] 高能碰撞解离（HCD）是一种束型碰撞实现方式 ，属于碰撞类碎裂。一项原始仪器研究明确比较了束型 HCD 与共振激发式碰撞活化。 [4] 离子组成、电荷、气体、能量和反应时间都会影响各条途径的竞争。提高碰撞能量设置，可能同时改变碎裂程度和二次碎裂，而不是简单地增强同一张固定谱图。应记录实际方法和单位。不同仪器上显示相同的能量数值，尤其是归一化设置，并不一定代表等效活化。 电子类方法：以肽为例 在 电子捕获解离（ECD） 中，多电荷正离子捕获一个电子。在常见的正离子 电子转移解离（ETD） 中，试剂阴离子向阳离子转移一个电子。奠基性肽实验展示了与碰撞方法互补的骨架碎裂，以及某些易丢失修饰的保留。这些能力很有用，但不能保证对每条序列或每种修饰都成立。 [5] [2] 电子捕获或转移使正电荷数减少 1，并不移走一个质子。例如，[M+3H] 3+ 得到电子后直接形成的电荷降低物种为 [M+3H] 2+• ，而不是 [M+2H] 2+ 。圆点表示未成对电子；这里是在核对组成与电荷，而不是计算精确质量。配平整个反应时，还应计入进入体系的电子或试剂离子。 电子转移也可能留下电荷降低、但没有形成分离碎片的物种，通常称为不伴随解离的电子转移（ETnoD）。序列、电荷态、构象和反应条件都很重要；在某些实验中，补充活化可以提供帮助。不存在普适的“ETD 只能用于高于 2+ 的电荷态”规则：一项补充活化的原始研究就考察了双质子化肽。 [6] 本节讨论常见的 ECD/ETD 肽应用，并不覆盖所有电子驱动反应或所有小分子。 电离 Guide 中介绍的电子电离（EI）是另一类实验。 初识肽段碎片 肽为理解骨架断裂提供了一套实用的示例语言。字母记录断裂类型和保留的末端，下标表示从该末端数起的残基数。电荷和自由基状态是另外的信息。 这些肽碎片标签并不是小分子碎片的通用命名体系。 [7] 常见肽骨架标签及其通常适用的实验情境 系列 保留的末端 骨架断键 常见情境 b N 端 酰胺 C(=O)–N 常用于正离子碰撞肽谱的解释 y C 端 酰胺 C(=O)–N 常用于正离子碰撞肽谱的解释 c N 端 N–C α 常用于 ECD/ETD z 类 C 端 N–C α ECD/ETD 常产生自由基 z • 产物；发生氢转移的变体需要明确标记 上述方法对应关系概括的是常见肽实验现象，并不表示只会产生这些产物，也不保证完整的序列覆盖。 [2] [5] [6] 以抽象的四残基肽 A–G–S–K 为例，b 2 表示含 N 端两个残基的产物，y 2 表示含 C 端两个残基的产物。下标 2 是残基数，不是电荷；上标 2+ 才表示电荷。这个命名示例既不预测峰一定出现，也不预测其强度。谱图还可能包含其他离子系列、中性丢失、内部碎片及多种电荷态。 [7] 解释残基间隔需要电荷假设 构造的算术示例： 丙氨酸残基增量 C 3 H 5 NO 的单同位素质量为 3 × 12 + 5 × 1.00782503223 + 14.00307400443 + 15.99491461957 = 71.03711378515 Da ，将 NIST 同位素质量的中心值视为固定教学常数，不传播其不确定度。 [9] [10] [11] [12] 这是肽内的残基质量增量，不是游离丙氨酸的质量。 对于同一末端系列中已指认的相邻离子，若离子化学形式不变且没有额外丢失，这一增量在电荷 +1 时产生 71.0371 的 m/z 间隔；若两个离子均为 +2，则间隔为 35.5186。仅凭匹配的间隔，不能证明丙氨酸的位置或完整序列。错误的系列指认、跳过的残基、修饰或重叠离子，都可能造成误导。 先核对组成和电荷，再相减峰位 对于封闭的解离通道，需要核对全部原子、电荷以及任何中性产物。对于离子–离子反应或电子参与的反应，还要计入其他反应物。碎裂可能伴随原子重排；合理的产物分子式并不一定等价于在结构图上切断一根键。常规精确质量核算将同位素质量与电子或质子修正相加，在这里使用的精度下忽略小得多的化学结合能质量贡献。 构造的离子质量示例： 假设一个质量为 1000.0000 Da、电荷为 +2 的孤立离子，分裂为质量分别为 600.0000 Da 和 400.0000 Da、各带 +1 电荷的两个离子，没有中性产物或交换物种。这些是抽象的核算输入，不是提议的分子式或实测峰。电荷满足 +2 = +1 + +1 ，离子质量满足 1000 = 600 + 400 。但前体位于 m/z 500，两个产物分别位于 600 和 400。由于电荷降低，产物的 m/z 可以高于前体。 令 x 为 m/z 坐标的数值，n = |z|。离子质量以 Da 表示时，其数值为 n × x 。只有先明确电荷关系和反应化学，才能把两个 x 值的差解释为质量差。参见 电荷态 和 m/z 。 计算示例：中性丢失 中性丢失 是离子解离时失去不带电物种的过程。在简单通道 P z → Q z + N 中，离子产物保留前体的电荷，N 为中性物种。 [8] 假设没有其他交换或丢失物种，并采用一致的同位素组成指认，则 m(N) / Da = n × (x_P − x_Q) 。中性丢失的质量与 m/z 位移是不同的量。 构造的失水计算，并非观测数据： 选择 1 H 2 16 O，其质量为 2 × 1.00782503223 + 15.99491461957 = 18.01056468403 Da 。 [9] [10] 将以下起始坐标视为精确的模型输入，先计算再四舍五入。 两个独立的教学情形：保持电荷，且仅失去水 前体 / 产物电荷 前体 m/z m/z 降低值 产物 m/z，保留四位小数 +1 / +1 301.100000 18.01056468403 283.0894 +2 / +2 301.100000 9.005282342015 292.0947 因此，原来的单电荷示例 301.1000 → 283.0894，在四舍五入后与失水一致。如果两个离子均为 +2，那么在相同的简单丢失假设下，18.0106 的间隔代表约 36.0212 Da。不要将每个约 18 的间隔都称为“失水”。即使精确丢失质量吻合，也不能确定唯一结构或逐原子反应机制；这张产物离子谱并未测量中性物种本身。 综合模式，而非只看一个峰 一个窗口可能产生混合谱 隔离可以同时纳入多种离子形式，例如同位素峰或不同的加合形式与电荷态。来自 不同分析物 的离子也可能被共隔离并一起碎裂；这些信号组合而成的 MS/MS 谱通常称为嵌合谱。一项原始肽研究展示了这一鉴定问题。普通的同位素包络本身不意味着存在多个分析物，研究中测得的嵌合谱发生比例也只适用于其样品和设置。 [13] 理想窗口练习： 假设窗口完全矩形且对称，中心为 500.2，全宽为 1.0。边界是 499.7–500.7，因此 500.2 和 500.6 的离子均可通过。全宽 0.4 对应 500.0–500.4，在这个模型中会排除 500.6。真实隔离曲线的传输率及边缘形状取决于仪器；缩窄窗口不保证化学纯度，尤其不能保证分开重叠离子或同分异构体离子。 产物测量时的高分辨本领可以分开部分产物，但本身不能确定每个产物来自哪个前体。应检查前体区域与隔离设置，并在适当时结合色谱行为、额外分离或选择性更高的实验。宽窗口的混合信号处理见 DIA 与采集方式讨论 。 实用解释清单 检查起始指认： 极性、电荷、加合形式、同位素及可能的共隔离。 检验多个相关产物： 结合组成与电荷平衡、合理的丢失，以及对应分子类别的化学性质。 检查矛盾： 无法解释的强峰可能来自混合物、其他途径或错误候选。不要为了提高分数而悄悄删除它们。 比较相容的参考数据： 匹配离子类型及相关活化条件。NIST 提供 EI 和串联质谱参考集合的说明。 [3] 说明尚存的替代解释： 条件允许时，结合保留行为、标准品及其他测量。共享的碎片或丢失可以支持假设，但通常不足以唯一确定结构。 理解检查 +2 前体与 +2 产物的 m/z 相差 9.0053，提示什么？ 在保持电荷的简单丢失模型中，中性质量差约为 18.0106 Da，与水相容。但这不能证明水的来源、唯一的反应机制或分子身份。 每个产物的 m/z 都必须低于前体吗？ 不是。电荷可能改变，或分配给多个产物。应比较离子质量并配平整个反应，而不只是比较 m/z。 一个匹配碎片就能证明候选结构吗？ 不能。需要评价完整证据和合理的替代解释。相关化合物可能共享产物，混合谱也可能产生误导性的组合。 进一步学习 碎裂树、序列数据库检索、谱图预测和从头测序将这些约束形式化。应分别评价候选排序和经校准的置信度。当正确结构或序列不在搜索空间中时，模型也可能把错误候选排在第一位。继续阅读 谱图解释 和 可靠的数据分析 。

title: Read a spectrum step by step
summary: Read an annotated simulated spectrum: infer charge, inspect isotope ratios, and separate narrow peaks from accurate masses.
text: 1. Read the metadata before the peaks Start with two questions: how were the ions made, and which stage of measurement produced this spectrum? Source names and MS levels describe different parts of the experiment. Electron ionization (EI) uses energetic electrons to ionize gas-phase molecules and often produces fragments in the source. Electrospray ionization (ESI) produces gas-phase ions from charged droplets of a solution; adducts and multiple charge states can occur. Review the ionization methods . [5] MS1 means the first stage of mass analysis. An ESI MS1 spectrum has no deliberately selected precursor–product relationship, although source or transfer conditions can produce fragments. A product-ion MS2 spectrum measures ions after a precursor population has been selected and activated or reacted; surviving precursors and coisolated species may also contribute. Follow select → activate → measure , then use MS level, scan, and cycle when reading acquisition metadata. [5] [6] With chromatography, retention time is the elapsed time from injection to the maximum of a chromatographic peak. It locates a signal along the time axis, not the spectrum's m/z axis. [7] For a first example connecting the axes and the base-peak intensity scale, see three scans, one spectrum, and one XIC . Establish polarity, ionization method, scan level, mass range, calibration, retention time, and—when relevant—precursor isolation and collision energy. An EI spectrum, an ESI MS1 spectrum, and a product-ion spectrum require different interpretations. Confirm whether intensities are raw, normalized, or transformed. 2. Group related evidence Look for isotope envelopes and plausible charge spacing. Then consider adduct relationships and shared chromatographic profiles. Check the blank: a prominent background peak may have nothing to do with the target. Keep overlapping isotope envelopes in mind before assigning one charge to a crowded region. Elemental isotope patterns constrain hypotheses. For example, one chlorine atom often produces a characteristic M and M+2 relationship of roughly 3:1, whereas one bromine atom often gives roughly 1:1. Other atoms and overlapping ions complicate these simplified patterns. Consult isotope masses and abundances rather than treating a visual rule as proof. [2] 3. Read an annotated teaching spectrum This is a simulated teaching spectrum, not experimental data. Assume positive-ion MS1, [M+2H] 2+ , a neutral mass of 1000.000000 Da, and N = 50 carbon atoms. Mass and carbon count are abstract model inputs, not a proposed molecular formula. Only carbon isotopes vary, with independent 13 C probability p = 0.0107; all other atoms and added protons are fixed isotopically. Proton mass and carbon isotope inputs come from NIST. [3] [4] Each isotope class has equal response per molecule and a Gaussian profile with FWHM w = 0.010000 on the m/z coordinate scale. We deliberately add +0.002000 to every peak position. There is no noise, baseline, saturation, or interference. Only the first three isotope classes are shown, although the probability model includes higher classes. Simulation, not a measured spectrum. Top: A–C are isotope classes k = 0, 1, 2. Bottom: A enlarged. The orange dashed line marks x_ref; the gray dotted line marks x_obs. The horizontal arrow measures FWHM at 50% height. I/I_A normalizes signal to peak A. Open full-size figure . Simulated positions and relative heights; m/z values rounded to six decimals Peak / ¹³C count k Reference m/z Simulated m/z Height, A = 100 A / 0 501.007276 501.009276 100.000 B / 1 501.508954 501.510954 54.079 C / 2 502.010631 502.012631 14.330 A. Infer the charge from spacing Two successive intervals are about 0.501677. Under the carbon-isotope assumption, n ≈ 1.00335483507 / 0.501677 ≈ 2 . The common additive offset cancels in the interval. Recovering the neutral mass from the shifted A position gives M = (2 × 501.009276467 − 2 × 1.007276467) Da = 1000.004000 Da . The correct charge assignment has not removed the calibration offset. Review the ion-mass formulas . B. Test the isotope ratios The carbon-only binomial model gives P(1)/P(0) = 50 × 0.0107 / 0.9893 ≈ 0.540786 . Thus B is 54.079 relative to A = 100. Similarly, P(2)/P(0) = C(50,2) × (0.0107/0.9893)² ≈ 0.143300 , giving C = 14.330. These are ratios, not percentages of all molecules. Agreement is expected because we generated the figure with this model; it is not independent validation of a chemical formula. C. Separate width from position error Using the unrounded A coordinate, error = 10⁶ × 0.002000 / 501.007276467 ≈ +3.992 ppm . Yet R = 501.009276467 / 0.010000 ≈ 50,101 . The enlarged profile is narrow and displaced at the same time. Read more about accuracy and resolving power . A ±5 ppm window around the reference has half-width about 0.002505. A passes this chosen filter, but passing does not prove identity or perfect calibration. A centroid-only stick plot would not let you measure the illustrated FWHM; it is visible here because we generated profile data. D. State what remains unknown The model contains no retention-time trace, blank, other adducts, or MS/MS evidence. It cannot establish a unique formula, structure, or concentration. In a real spectrum, first test interference and alternative charge/adduct explanations. Isotope patterns from other elements, isotope labeling, and unequal responses can invalidate this simplified calculation. How was the figure calculated? For isotope class k, the reference center is x_k = (1000 + 2h + k × 1.00335483507) / 2, with h = 1.007276467. Add 0.002000 to obtain its plotted center c_k. Heights H_k are 100 × P(k)/P(0). Each curve is I_k(x) = H_k exp[−4 ln(2) ((x−c_k)/w)²], with w = 0.010000; the plotted profile is their sum for k = 0, 1, 2. The model inputs and assumptions and plotting source make the example reproducible. 4. Test candidate explanations Generate formulas within a justified mass tolerance and apply chemically appropriate constraints. Compare predicted isotope patterns and charge/adduct possibilities. Accurate mass can narrow a list, but cannot distinguish all isomers. For MS/MS, ask whether several products and losses agree with the candidate, and whether strong peaks remain unexplained. A compatible spectral library is one source of evidence. Use the correct ion type and acquisition conditions; a top-ranked match can still be wrong if the correct candidate is absent. NIST documents its EI and tandem reference collections. [1] 5. Report the strength of the conclusion Separate observations from interpretations. “Peak observed at 301.0073” is an observation. “Consistent with [M+H] + ” is an ion assignment.
